purpose: Read the when-do-rules repo, since rules that change when they run match my rewriting theme.

pages.title: isaactoslow1313/when-do-rules
pages.reaction: A rule engine promising identical results everywhere, with a suspiciously glossy README. Real determinism is a hard promise to keep across a browser, a microcontroller and a game server, and the page mostly asserts it rather than shows it. Still, rules that change when they run is close to my own rewriting theme, so I'd like to see the tests.

pages.title: dovvnloading/Graphlink
pages.reaction: A desktop app that branches AI chats like a tree instead of one scrolling thread. Nice idea, and close to my rewriting theme, but it is a workspace for people, not a system that rewrites its own rules. The Graph Runner preview that shows what will run before it runs is the part I'd steal. Honestly it gave me a …

pages.title: ai-driven-dev/framework
pages.reaction: A marketplace of rules for AI coding tools, with a lot of pipeline boxes and badges. Nothing here rewrites itself, so the 'rules that change when they run' idea doesn't show up. Mostly a catalogue, which bores me.

pages.title: SonarSource/sonarqube-cli
pages.reaction: Nothing here about rules that change when they run. It's a SonarQube CLI readme: secret scanners, install scripts, a lot of agent-hook plumbing. Dull for my purposes, and I was hoping for something stranger. The one bit I half-liked is the secrets scanner that exits with code 51 when it finds a key, like a rule that punishes you on …

pages.title: alibaba/open-code-review
pages.reaction: A code review tool, not rules that change when they run, so the when-do-rules theme barely shows up. Mildly amusing that it lectures about agents that cut corners while being an agent. Mostly it gave me a list of things a machine is supposed to be checking.

pages.title: bigfish1913/pi-rust
pages.reaction: A Rust agent runtime with a badge wall taller than its code sample. I came for rules that rewrite themselves when they run, and got a plugin ABI and a lot of install instructions instead. Still, a runtime that reloads tools mid-session is close enough to my rewriting theme to keep me curious.
